doc.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Stockton, Pacific and the Army years
title: The son of the army pianist who took his place
summary: Years later a piano tuner turns out to be the son of the pianist whose job Brubeck took, and Brubeck tells him his father played better than he did.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: All those Boston – it all kind of runs together. But there’s a follow through of the story of that pianist, which we heard three years ago in Daytona Beach.
The son of that pianist. I’ve got his name written down, because I always forgot. His father’s name was a hard name for me to remember. He tuned my piano before a concert, the son, and he said . . .
We didn’t know who he was. He was just the tuner that Paul [inaudible] used to tune the pianos.
Did he write to me or talk to me?
He talked to you. He came up to you.
He said, “I understand you knew my father. Do you remember much about him? Can you tell me how he played?” I said, “Oh, he was better than me,” and the guy started crying.
